overview: This Senate resolution congratulates Mississippi Christian University, in Clinton, Mississippi, on its 200th anniversary. Founded in 1826 as Hampstead Academy and long known as Mississippi College, it is the oldest college in Mississippi and was renamed on June 1, 2026. The resolution recounts milestones, including its claim to be the first coeducational college in the country to grant degrees to women, in 1831, and the later addition of nursing, law, and physician assistant programs. It recognizes the school's faith-based academic, community, and athletic work and asks that copies be sent to its leaders. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on July 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution fittingly honors two centuries of education and service by the state's oldest college.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic, singles out a single private institution, and does not change any law or spending.
